replies.author: shlaifu
replies.body:
I think the problem is one of language. My native language differentiates between what in English is called 'fine art' and creative expression etc., and what in English is called 'commercial art' or design. Games aren't artworks in these usage, but products. Artists aren't artists (no one would call a character or level designer or even a concept artist an artist in my language) but designers who are hired to facilitate the creation of a product. In that context, the use of AI is obviously widespread at this point.

Indie game developers see themselves as artist-artists and their games as artworks, not strictly as products. To look at a multi-million dollar production and even think about it as an artwork is the delusional part.

comments.author: Takezo_00
comments.body:
Former game dev from a work for hire indie studio.
Can confirm. All programmers used copilot to speed up code generation. Artists used AI for art direction mocks/inspiration.  We weren’t shipping games with AI art but it’s an integrated part of the pipeline for sure.

replies.author: PuteMorte

replies.author: Takezo_00
replies.body: I agree. And what people don't realize is that while, yes... AI takes away work from programmers in a technical sense since it's that much less code that has to be written upfront anyway, that it also enables developers to super rapidly prototype something that would have eaten resources, meaning that prototype idea that sunk $50k in man hours between the 5 man prototyping team on an idea that doesn't go into production get's re-allocated elsewhere -- hopefully into pension plans or raises or simply keeping the lights on in these smaller studios in an industry that's a total meat grinder right now in part because of AI, sure, but in part in-spite of it.

replies.author: Mean_Establishment31
replies.body: Also, a game dev. Can confirm it is becoming just a normal part of the workflow. It’s everywhere for everything from automatic meeting notes, automatic bug searching and hypothesis generation as to what the fix should be, previs mocks, complex system tutorials, Slack agents connecting threads and messaging updates, early stage ideation inspiration, robo-VO, design documentation, etc. Never part of the final product,m, but yeah, it’s at every single stage of development now.

replies.author: Takezo_00
replies.body: And I mean, I understand why that’s concerning because people used to have to do most of those things and now they don’t. But the flip side is that devs can iterate 10x faster in the early stages, proofing radical ideas way faster, that would otherwise eat up tons of resources before a concept ever gets greenlit (and often doesn’t for that exact reason)

replies.author: Mean_Establishment31
